title: Developer Experience Documentation: SDK Guides, Quickstarts & Templates, API Examples, Docs Site Ops, and Top Support Issues
author: Alex Chen
body:
Summary
This document describes the standards, templates, and operating procedures used by the Developer Experience (DevEx) team for producing SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs site runbooks, and the canonical fixes for the top support issues. It is intended for DevEx authors, technical writers, SDK owners, and engineering reviewers.

Goals
- Provide consistent, discoverable, and executable SDK guides and quickstarts that reduce time-to-first-success for new users.
- Surface canonical API examples that are accurate, minimal, and tested against CI.
- Define docs site operating procedures to ensure timely reviews, releases, and rollback policies.
- Maintain a prioritized list of top support issues with reproducible fixes and one-line mitigations for on-call responders.

Audience and Scope
- Audience: SDK engineers, technical writers, solutions engineers, onboarding specialists, and support engineers.
- Scope: All first-party SDKs (Python, Node, Go, Java), official quickstart repositories, API examples embedded in docs, and the public docs site content maintained by DevEx. This excludes experimental community-contributed examples (those live in community repos and must be labeled as such).

Naming and File Conventions
- File names should be lowercase, dash-separated, and end with a year when applicable: `sdk-python-quickstart-2026.md`.
- Each guide must start with a one-line summary and a 3–5 item prerequisites list.
- Example files included with quickstarts must use permissive headers and include `LICENSE` and `NOTICE` when bundling third-party code.

Structure for SDK Guides (required sections)
1) Title and one-line summary
2) Audience and prerequisites (OS, language version, auth method)
3) Installation and quick start snippet (copy-paste runnable)
4) Conceptual overview (objects and workflows, e.g., Client, Request, Streaming)
5) Minimal examples (sync, async, streaming if applicable)
6) Error handling and retries (with example code)
7) Configuration reference (table of common config keys and defaults)
8) Troubleshooting (common errors and short mitigations)
9) Links to API reference, LICENSE, changelog, and contribution guide

Example: minimal Python quickstart snippet (to be included verbatim)
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=REDSHIFT_API_KEY)
resp = client.generate("Write a one-paragraph summary of Redwood Inference")
print(resp.text)
```

Quickstarts & Templates (pattern and locations)
- Canonical quickstarts live in the `devex/quickstarts` monorepo and are mirrored on docs.redwood.ai/quickstarts. Each quickstart must include: `README.md`, `example/.env.example`, `Makefile` with `make run` and `make test`, and a lightweight integration test under `tests/` that runs in CI.
- Templates: The public quickstart template must be used for all new quickstarts. Template includes: `01-getting-started.md`, `02-api-examples.md`, `03-best-practices.md`, `sample-config.yaml`, and `smoke-test.sh`.
- Quickstart lifecycle: create -> author review -> security scan -> CI smoke test -> publish. See Docs Site Operating Procedures below for timing SLAs.

API Examples: Best Practices
- Keep examples short (10–30 lines) and focused on a single task. Avoid multi-file examples unless demonstrating multi-step workflows.
- All examples referenced in docs must be runnable against an ephemeral test key in CI. We run examples via `docs-examples-ci` which executes snippets and fails the build on output mismatch or exceptions.
- Provide both minimal and production variants where appropriate: `example.min.py` and `example.prod.py`. The production variant should demonstrate batching, retries, and observability hooks.
- Include input/output assertions in examples used by tests.

Docs Site Operating Procedures (authoring -> publish workflow)
1) Author submits a branch with draft page(s) and fills out the docs PR template (title, summary, reviewer, tests added, affected SDKs).
2) Automated checks run: link-checker, spell-checker, example-runner, security-scan.
3) DevEx reviewer has 48 business hours to provide feedback. If no review, ping rotating on-call reviewer after 48 hours.
4) After sign-off, merge to `main-docs`. Merge triggers staging deploy and integration smoke tests.
5) Staging must pass smoke tests within 2 hours, otherwise the release is marked `blocked`.
6) Production deploy occurs on next scheduled docs release window (daily at 03:00 UTC) unless the change is security-critical.
7) Rollback: any production regression detected within 24 hours triggers an automatic rollback to the previous version and the author/owner-team is paged.

Ownership and SLAs
- Each major page must list an `owner` (person) and `owner_team` in the page metadata header. Owner is responsible for accuracy and responding to reviewer comments.
- SLAs: critical doc bugs (page broken, examples failing) — page owner notified within 15 minutes via PagerDuty; fix or mitigation within 4 hours. Non-critical content updates — re-review within 5 business days.

Top Support Issues (current top 10) and Canonical Fixes
Note: The list below is derived from support tickets and triage sessions (Q4 2025–Q1 2026). Each entry includes: symptom, root cause, canonical fix, and one-line mitigation for on-call.
1) Authentication errors: `401` or `invalid API key`
   - Root cause: using the wrong environment key (staging vs production) or missing `REDWOOD_API_KEY` in environment.
   - Canonical fix: Update quickstart README to include exact env var instructions and add validation on client instantiation that emits an actionable error if key missing.
   - On-call mitigation: Ask user to run `echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY` and confirm; provide temporary test key if needed.
2) Streaming responses hang or close prematurely
   - Root cause: network proxies or missing `read_timeout` in SDK streaming client.
   - Canonical fix: Update SDK docs with recommended socket/read timeouts, and add retry/backoff example in streaming quickstart.
   - On-call mitigation: Suggest `curl` test and recommend `--no-buffer` in proxy for immediate troubleshooting.
3) Slow cold-start latency for Dedicated deployments in quickstarts
   - Root cause: using large model variant in default quickstart without specifying `instance_type` or `warmup_tokens`.
   - Canonical fix: Change quickstart defaults to a balanced model and include `warmup()` snippet in examples.
   - On-call mitigation: Recommend switching to a lite model or enabling prefix cache in request.
4) Rate limit (429) confusion
   - Root cause: unclear guidance on tenant-level quotas and SDK client retry behavior.
   - Canonical fix: Document default quotas in quickstart and include example of exponential backoff and `Retry-After` handling.
   - On-call mitigation: Advise transient retry with backoff and suggest client-side rate limiter.
5) Embeddings mismatch or small numeric differences causing failing similarity tests
   - Root cause: model variant mismatch or quantization differences across environments.
   - Canonical fix: Pin model versions in example tests and add numeric tolerance in assertion helpers.
   - On-call mitigation: Ask user to confirm model id and float precision; run `pip install redwood-utils==stable` to align helpers.
6) Confusing error messages from invalid function/tool calls in chat examples
   - Root cause: examples using deprecated `tool` schema.
   - Canonical fix: Update examples to function-calling schema, add migration note, and include a validation tool in `docs-examples-ci`.
   - On-call mitigation: Share the migration snippet and link to the function-calling migration guide.
7) SDK installation failures on older Node versions
   - Root cause: package requires modern Node features not present in Node 12.x in user environments.
   - Canonical fix: Add engines field to package.json, update quickstart prerequisites, and publish a legacy compatibility note.
   - On-call mitigation: Ask user to run `node -v`; recommend `nvm install --lts`.
8) Misconfigured CORS for browser quickstarts
   - Root cause: demo servers run without proper Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers.
   - Canonical fix: Provide secure CORS config in quickstart template with explicit allowed origins and a dev-mode toggle.
   - On-call mitigation: Ask user to test with `curl -I` and provide the minimal CORS header snippet.
9) Examples failing due to missing feature flags or account entitlements
   - Root cause: some features (dedicated capacity, private deployment) require account enablement.
   - Canonical fix: Add a short feature-check step in quickstarts that queries account capabilities and prints a helpful error.
   - On-call mitigation: Check account feature flags and open an admin enablement ticket if required.
10) Outdated examples after SDK surface changes
   - Root cause: breaking changes without cross-team coordination.
   - Canonical fix: Enforce SDK release checklist that includes updating docs examples and add a pre-release docs smoke test job.
   - On-call mitigation: Provide the migration guide and a patch PR template that updates example code.

Canonical Fix Deliverables and Tracking
- For each top issue, create a short-lived tracking epic in the `devex` board and assign an owner. Epic should include: updated quickstart file, passing example smoke test, and an entry in the changelog.
- Use the `docs-fixes` label on PRs that implement canonical fixes. Owners should reference the support ticket ID in PR description for traceability.

Testing and CI Requirements
- Every example must be covered by at least one automated test in `docs-examples-ci`. Tests must run in < 60s wherever possible.
- Security scans must run on quickstart repos and block merges on flagged secrets or unsafe exec calls.
- Flaky tests must be annotated with `flaky=true` in CI and have a corresponding follow-up ticket.

Templates (copyable snippets)
- Page metadata header (add to top of each markdown page):
```
---
title: "Page Title"
owner: "Alice Example"
owner_team: "developer-experience"
labels: ["sdk","quickstart"]
---
```
- PR checklist for docs changes (must be included in PR description):
  - [ ] Title & summary present
  - [ ] Examples added/updated and covered by CI tests
  - [ ] Security scan passed
  - [ ] Reviewer assigned
  - [ ] Changelog entry (if user-facing)

Monitoring and Metrics
- Track the following KPIs monthly: time-to-first-success (median time from signup to successful sample run), docs CI pass rate, top-10 support issue volume, and docs page engagement (views and time-on-page).
- Use the DevEx dashboard in Grafana (dash id: devex-docs-001) to visualize trends and regressions.

Retention and Review Cadence
- All quickstarts: review frequency 6 months.
- API examples embedded in stable pages: review frequency 3 months.
- Deprecated examples: mark with `deprecated: true` and provide migration notes; remove after 12 months if no usage.

Appendix: Troubleshooting checklist for on-call
1) Reproduce locally using `docs-examples-ci` container image.
2) Collect logs: example stdout/stderr, request ids, and `X-Request-Id` headers.
3) Check the example run against the pinned model version and SDK version.
4) If failure is environment-specific, provide a minimal repro gist and open a triage ticket with `devex-team` label.

Contact and Escalation
- DevEx rotations: `devex-oncall@redwood.ai` (primary), `devex-sre@redwood.ai` (secondary).
- For legal/security issues discovered in examples, immediately escalate to `security@redwood.ai` and mark the PR `security-blocker`.

Revision History
- 2025-11-10: Initial draft by Alex Chen.
- 2026-01-08: Added CI example-runner requirements and streaming timeout guidance (reviewers: Priya N.).
- 2026-03-15: Published with top-10 support issues and canonical fixes (reviewers: Diego Morales, Samira Patel).

End of document
